preamble: Vocalization of the rhotic [r] to the high front vowel [i] or palatal glide [j]. In Cibaeño Dominican Spanish, syllable-final /ɾ/ (and /l/) is vocalized to [j], so hacer is [aˈsej] and cerda 'bristle' merges with celda 'cell' as [ˈsejða]. A related historical case is Middle Indo-Aryan: the Sanskrit syllabic rhotic ṛ [r̩] often became the vowel i in Pali (ṛṣi > isi 'sage'), alongside outcomes a and u.

examples.note: Syllable-final /ɾ/ vocalizes to a palatal glide in the Cibao region.
Coda /ɾ/ and /l/ neutralize to [j], so cerda and celda 'cell' become homophones.
The syllabic rhotic ṛ became i; ṣ also became s.
ṛ > i after a palatal; ś also became s.
